headline: Dry weather and increasingly cool nights settle into Central Kentucky while light rain and fog give way to a cooler, drier Upstate
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: A weak disturbance departs while continental high pressure builds into the Ohio Valley. Central Kentucky stays dry through Tuesday, with partial clearing today, a breezy and cooler Monday, and sunny conditions Tuesday. Clearer skies and verified local cold biases support chilly nighttime ranges, especially around Danville and in sheltered valleys.

days.label: Sunday
days.forecast: Morning clouds around Danville gradually thin, while Lexington and the northern Bluegrass see more sunshine. The afternoon is dry with a light north to northeast breeze around 4–8 mph. Temperatures reach the middle or upper 70s. Skies become mostly clear tonight, allowing readings to fall into the upper 40s, with the coldest rural pockets near the middle 40s.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: A few sheltered valleys may approach the upper 30s Monday night
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and less humid beneath building high pressure. Northeast winds increase to about 8–13 mph during the afternoon, with occasional gusts near 17 mph. Highs stay mainly in the lower to middle 70s, though warmer global guidance supports the upper end of the range. Clear skies and light winds Monday night favor strong cooling into the lower 40s and locally upper 30s.

days.label: Tuesday
days.forecast: Sunny and dry with a light east to southeast breeze. The NWS and NAM favor the lower or middle 70s, while GFS and ECMWF guidance is several degrees warmer, so the temperature range remains deliberately broad. Tuesday night stays clear and cool, with rural locations again several degrees colder than urban Lexington.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky has a quiet three-day period ahead. Rain is not expected, humidity falls, and afternoons remain comfortable. The main forecast detail is nighttime cooling: upper 40s tonight, lower 40s Monday night and locally upper 30s in sheltered valleys, followed by another cool Tuesday night.
kentucky.confidence: High on dry weather and cool nights; moderate on Tuesday's high because GFS and ECMWF guidance is warmer than the NWS and NAM

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson / Central primary · Tempest excluded
upstate.summary: A cool, stable wedge keeps Clemson and Central cloudy with periods of mainly light rain or drizzle today. Rain fades tonight, but saturated low levels may produce fog into Monday morning. Partial clearing and a warmer afternoon follow Monday, then renewed northeast flow brings a cooler, breezy and dry Tuesday.

currentConditions.condition: Network observations are WeatherFlow–Tempest-fed and excluded; official KCEU and KLQK observations used instead

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: Reduced visibility in drizzle and fog is the main concern; the earlier excessive-rain threat has ended
days.forecast: Cloudy and cool beneath a shallow northeast-flow wedge. Mainly light rain and drizzle become more common this afternoon and evening, but weak forcing and stable air should keep totals modest and thunderstorms are not expected around Clemson. Rain diminishes overnight. Low clouds and fog may develop late, with locally dense fog possible toward Monday morning.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: Patchy fog may reduce visibility during the morning commute
days.forecast: Patchy fog and low clouds linger through part of the morning, then gradual drying allows breaks of sunshine. Temperatures recover into the middle or upper 70s, although a slower wedge erosion would keep some locations near the lower end of the range. Monday night becomes mostly clear and cooler; sheltered KLQK-area valleys may fall close to 50.

days.label: Tuesday
days.hazard: Northeast gusts near 20 mph are possible during the afternoon
days.forecast: Dry with considerable sunshine, but a renewed northeast breeze keeps temperatures cooler. Winds increase to around 7–12 mph with occasional gusts near 20 mph. NAM guidance holds a much stronger cool wedge than GFS and ECMWF, so the high-temperature range is wider than usual. Mostly clear conditions follow Tuesday night, with KLQK and other cold pockets reaching the middle or upper 40s.

upstate.bottomLine: Light rain and drizzle—not heavy thunderstorms—are the main story today. Rain ends tonight, followed by a fog risk early Monday. Monday becomes drier and warmer, while Tuesday is sunny, breezy and cooler under renewed northeast flow. No official NWS alerts were active at issuance.
upstate.confidence: High on today's cloudy and mainly light-rain pattern and the transition to dry weather Monday; moderate on Tuesday temperatures because NAM retains a substantially stronger cool wedge than GFS and ECMWF

sourceNotes: Official airport observations span 9:20–9:50 AM EDT, and the NWS point forecasts were generated at approximately 10:04 AM EDT. The Kentucky forecast grid was updated at 4:02 AM EDT and the Upstate grid at 8:03 AM EDT.

The Louisville and Greenville-Spartanburg Area Forecast Discussions were issued at 6:52 AM and 6:41 AM EDT, respectively. Louisville supports dry weather, upper-70s warmth today, cooler and breezier conditions Monday and chilly Monday night. Greenville-Spartanburg states that the earlier excessive-rain threat has ended, with mainly light rain or drizzle today, fog possible tonight and dry weather returning Monday.

The NWS active-alert API returned no active alerts for either the Danville or Clemson forecast point at the approximately 10:04 AM EDT check. This official alert status is separate from the independent discussion of fog and locally reduced visibility.

Model inventories checked at approximately 10:04 AM EDT showed the complete 12Z HRRR through forecast hour 48, complete 09Z RAP through hour 51, 06Z NAM through hour 84, 06Z NAM 3-km Nest through hour 60, 06Z GFS and GEFS mean through hour 384, and 06Z ECMWF through hour 144. Partial newer cycles were not substituted for complete cycles beyond their available range.

College of DuPage NEXLAB radar at 9:55 AM EDT showed scattered areas of rain across the Southeast rather than an organized heavy-rain corridor over either forecast area. Clean-infrared satellite imagery at 9:56 AM EDT showed an extensive cloud and moisture shield across the Gulf states and Carolinas, consistent with persistent Upstate clouds and more variable cloud cover across Kentucky.

College of DuPage model panels agree on a dry Monday but diverge materially Tuesday. NAM keeps a strong cool wedge in the Upstate and holds Kentucky in the middle 70s, while GFS and ECMWF are several degrees warmer in both regions. Forecast ranges were widened rather than forcing either extreme solution.

Clemson Weather Network identifies its observations as WeatherFlow–Tempest data. Those observations were excluded, and official KCEU and KLQK observations were used for Upstate analysis and verification.

The forecast-accuracy summary generated at 9:58 AM EDT was consulted from main. KDVK and KLEX low-temperature ranges were shifted lower using the documented minus 2 to minus 2.5 degree recommendations. The KLQK minus 4 degree low bias was represented by widening Upstate nighttime ranges downward rather than applying it to the entire region. Ranges were widened at 24 and 72 hours because verified coverage remains below 50 percent at those lead times, and small residual precipitation probabilities were retained because the 0–20 percent bin has observed precipitation slightly more often than forecast.
Radar, satellite and model-image links are timestamped external references. The existing website radar section is not modified by this candidate.

appliedAdjustments.details: Shifted overnight ranges roughly 2–2.5°F lower in response to the verified KDVK and KLEX low-temperature biases, while keeping daytime ranges centered on current guidance because the high-temperature biases remain below the correction threshold. Widened the day-one and day-three ranges because coverage at 24 and 72 hours remains below 50 percent.

Widened nighttime ranges downward to represent KLQK's verified cold-pocket bias without imposing the full 4°F station correction across Clemson and KCEU. Widened Tuesday's high range to preserve the large NAM-versus-GFS/ECMWF wedge spread.
